title: Magnetar brings faster, simpler, quantum-ready zero-knowledge proofs
gist: Microsoft Research presents Magnetar, a RISC-V zero-knowledge virtual machine that proves ordinary Rust/Go/C programs 10 to 39 times faster than the prior fastest comparable zkVMs while relying only on standard hash functions (no trusted setup, elliptic curves or lattices). Microsoft frames it as the point where practical, quantum-safe proofs of execution become a routine output of computation.

themes.theme: Zero-knowledge proofs as a trust primitive

insights.claim: A zero-knowledge proof lets a program return, alongside its output, a short certificate that the program ran correctly on given inputs, which anyone can verify in milliseconds without rerunning it or trusting the operator.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Shifts verification from trusting operators, vendors or counterparties to checking a cheap cryptographic artifact; watch for products that replace audits and logs with proofs.

insights.claim: Zero-knowledge proofs could let an AI agent attach a proof that each action complied with its assigned policy, and let regulated financial institutions prove transactions were processed correctly without making them public.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Agent accountability and private regulatory compliance are the demand-side use cases to track for verifiable computing.
insights.quote: A result no longer has to be trusted because of who produced it. It can be checked because of what accompanies it.

insights.claim: Microsoft expects technology leaders to stop asking whether proofs of execution are practical and to focus instead on which results they would rather verify than take on trust.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Signals Microsoft positioning verifiable computing as an enterprise category, not a crypto niche.

insights.claim: Proof generation has historically cost millions of times more computation than running the program itself, and the fastest systems bought speed through compromises elsewhere.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Proving overhead is the main economic constraint; step-change speedups change which workloads are viable.

insights.claim: Many proof systems force developers to hand-rewrite programs as fixed cryptographic circuits, which takes months, must be redone for every change, and is a frequent source of security bugs.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Circuit-authoring skill scarcity limits adoption; zkVMs that accept compiled code remove that bottleneck.
insights.locator: Three grand challenges - Generality and usability

insights.claim: Many existing proof systems rest on elliptic curves that a sufficiently powerful quantum computer could break, while post-quantum alternatives often rely on lattice assumptions, newly invented hash-like functions, or unproven conjectures about error-correcting codes.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Quantum-exposed proof systems face a future migration; hash-only designs are the conservative hedge.

insights.claim: Microsoft's Quantum Safe Program will move its products and services to post-quantum cryptography, a goal it recently accelerated to 2029.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: A 2029 target from a hyperscaler sets a practical timeline for post-quantum migration demand.

insights.claim: Microsoft Research's decade-long line of work (Spartan in 2019, Phalanx, Nova and successors, Brakedown, Lasso/Twist and Shout, Jolt-style processor proving, Vega, BinarySpartan) supplied the separate pieces that Magnetar combines.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Shows Magnetar is an integration of years of building blocks, suggesting a durable Microsoft IP position in verifiable computing.
insights.quote: Each of these solved a piece of the problem. Magnetar is where the pieces come together.
insights.locator: More than a decade of work

insights.claim: Spartan (2019) revived the sum-check approach for general-purpose programs without a trusted setup, and its flexibility over cryptographic building blocks is what later allowed a hash-only construction.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Explains why trusted-setup-free designs were possible, relevant for assessing alternatives to SNARK systems needing secret setup.
insights.locator: More than a decade of work

insights.claim: Vega applied this line of work to digital identity, proving facts from a government credential in under a tenth of a second.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Digital-identity credentials are an early concrete application for private proofs.
insights.locator: More than a decade of work

insights.claim: Magnetar is a zkVM that proves execution of the open RISC-V architecture, so developers can write in Rust, Go or C, compile as usual, and have programs proven as written, making proving no longer a specialist activity.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: General-purpose RISC-V proving widens the developer pool able to use proofs, including for EVM interpreters and data pipelines.

insights.claim: Magnetar proves 7.2 to 8.7 million processor instructions per second on a laptop, is 10 to 39 times faster on average across 15 benchmarks than the fastest existing zkVMs on the same machine, and more than 300 times faster than two others on a token-transfer benchmark.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Vendor-reported benchmarks; independent replication versus incumbent zkVMs is the thing to watch.
insights.locator: Magnetar - It is faster than prior systems

insights.claim: An optimized Magnetar proves 9.5-12.8 million cycles per second, raising each reported speedup by about 1.3x, and its proofs verify in about 12 milliseconds.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Millisecond verification makes on-chain or edge verification plausible.
insights.locator: Magnetar - It is faster than prior systems

insights.claim: Magnetar's security depends only on a standard hash function such as SHA-256 or SHA-3, with no elliptic curves, lattices, special-purpose hash functions, trusted setup, or unproven coding-theory conjecture, which removes a future cryptographic migration from the roadmap.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Hash-only security is the most conservative post-quantum bet and a differentiator against conjecture-based zkVMs.
insights.quote: relying only on standard hash functions removes a cryptographic migration from the roadmap
insights.locator: Magnetar - Its security rests on standard cryptography

insights.claim: Because verifying a Magnetar proof consists mostly of hash evaluations and binary-field arithmetic, which Magnetar itself proves efficiently, it can prove computations of any size by proving pieces and combining them, including long-running systems such as a ledger or blockchain.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Recursion-friendly design points to applicability for rollups and ledgers.
insights.locator: Magnetar - Its security rests on standard cryptography
